rows.title: CT comptroller to lawmakers: Don’t stray far from fiscal guardrails
rows.standfirst: Despite CT’s $1.9 billion surplus, Comptroller Sean Scanlon warned lawmakers that “the budget will not always remain as it is today.”

rows.title: CT lawmakers want more property tax relief for qualifying veterans
rows.standfirst: The relief program, which hasn’t been overhauled since shortly after the Civil War, could save qualifying veterans $2,000 on property taxes.

rows.title: CT energy assistance needs more state funding, advocates say
rows.standfirst: With federal heating assistance projected to drop and oil prices rising, advocates say CT officials should use state funds for heating aid.

rows.title: CT’s richest should pay more tax on investment income, senator says
rows.standfirst: A “growing disparity” in earnings means higher taxes on high-earners’ investment income makes sense, according to Sen. Martin Looney.

rows.title: Construction ramps up in fall. CT still lost 900 jobs in September
rows.standfirst: The loss ranked among the worst of any state, and it came at a time when employment normally ramps up to finish projects before winter.

rows.title: Another looming fiscal challenge in CT: State retiree health care
rows.standfirst: Connecticut’s health care program for retired state workers shifts hundreds of millions of dollars in costs into the future, analysts say.

rows.title: More heating aid proposed; still less for CT families than last winter
rows.standfirst: The proposed boost in heating aid would still leave CT families with less than last winter, and advocates say the state should contribute.
